title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 60–62 of the manuscript): L/K is a field extension, e.g. a function field over a field K of finite type over Q. 𝓔_L and 𝓔_K are the Galois categories (étale toposes) of L and K. Grothendieck is looking for (germs of) sections of 𝓔_L → 𝓔_K, i.e. sections of Gal(L̄/L) → Gal(K̄/K) defined over open subgroups. He uses the 'Riemann variety' 𝓧 = lim X of L/K, meaning the Zariski–Riemann space of valuation rings of L containing K.

This page, step by step:

1. Take a valuation ring O ⊃ K of L, i.e. a point x of 𝓧. Let O' be its normalisation in L̄, equivalently the normalisation S' of S in L. For x' over x one has a decomposition group N_{x'} and an inertia group I_{x'}. The interpretations found earlier for a special kind of O carry over.

2. The key idea. When O has 'simple structure', I read this as a discrete valuation of rank α in residue characteristic 0, so value group Z^α. Then:
   - The inertia group is T^α, where T = T(L̄) = Ẑ(1) is the Tate module (marginal note T_α = T_α(L̄)).
   - α is the 'codimension' of x in 𝓧.
   - The decomposition group is an extension of Gal(k(x)) by T^α, where k(x) is the residue field.

3. If x is a point of dimension 0, then k(x) is finite over K. So Gal(k(x)) is an open subgroup of Gal(K) (a finite étale K-group), and it acts on T^α through the cyclotomic character. In characteristic 0 the tame extension 1 → T^α → N_{x'} → Gal(k(x)) → 1 splits. A splitting is obtained by choosing 'parameters', i.e. uniformisers or a compatible system of roots of them (the 'choix de pointes/paramètres').

4. Each such splitting gives a germ of section of 𝓔_L over 𝓔_K. The next page states the conclusion: 'un principe général pour construction des germes de sections de 𝓔_L sur 𝓔_K à l'aide des pts de dim 0 de la variété de Riemann de L sur K'.

5. Next page: for a transcendence-degree-1 subextension L_1, composing with 𝓔_L → 𝓔_{L_1} gives sections of 𝓔_{L_1}. One might hope to find more than the sections attached to places of L_1/K, but V ∩ L_1 is again a valuation ring, so no new ones arise.

In short, this is the construction of 'valuation-theoretic' or 'cuspidal / tangential' sections that underlies the birational section conjecture, done here for higher transcendence degree via rank-α valuations (flags, Parshin-chain type) of the Zariski–Riemann space.
errors: The statement 'inertia ≅ T^α' only holds for valuations whose value group is Z^α (discrete of rank α, 'structure simple') and whose residue characteristic is 0. For general points of the Zariski–Riemann space the value group need not be finitely generated, and in residue characteristic p there is wild inertia. Grothendieck seems aware of this ('à structure simple').

Identifying α with the 'codimension' of x in 𝓧 is natural for Abhyankar valuations whose residue field is finite over K. In general, rational rank can differ from the codimension/rank, so the formula needs that hypothesis.

The splitting of the decomposition group is not canonical: sections come in families (torsors under H^1(k(x), T^α)), as Grothendieck's 'choix' suggests. This is not a gap, but each valuation yields a packet of germs of sections, not a single one.

ideas.what: Decomposition/inertia groups of a valuation ring of L containing K, via normalisation in L̄
ideas.modern_name: decomposition and inertia groups of valuations (ramification theory for Krull valuations)

ideas.what: For a discrete rank-α valuation in residue characteristic 0, inertia ≅ Ẑ(1)^α, and the decomposition group is a split extension of Gal(k(x)) by it
ideas.modern_name: tame inertia of Z^α-valued valuations; structure of decomposition groups
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical; used systematically in birational anabelian geometry by Pop, Bogomolov–Tschinkel

ideas.what: Constructing germs of sections of Gal(L) → Gal(K) from dimension-0 points of the Zariski–Riemann space of L/K (valuations with residue field finite over K), by splitting decomposition groups
ideas.modern_name: sections arising from valuations / cuspidal or tangential sections; Parshin-chain sections; birational section conjecture in higher dimension
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck's letter to Faltings (1983) for the conjecture; Koenigsmann (2005), Pop (birational p-adic section conjecture), Stix (cuspidal sections, packets), Esnault–Wittenberg for the valuation-theoretic sections
ideas.where_published: The section conjecture, including a birational variant, is in the letter to Faltings (1983); the higher-dimensional Zariski–Riemann formulation is not known to me in his published texts.

ideas.what: Observation that for a transcendence-degree-1 subfield L_1, sections induced from valuations of L give nothing beyond those from places of L_1 (V ∩ L_1 is a valuation ring)
ideas.modern_name: compatibility of valuation sections with restriction to subfields
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore in birational section conjecture literature

missed.claim: Grothendieck formulates a general principle: germs of sections of Gal(L) → Gal(K) for a function field L of arbitrary transcendence degree come from dimension-0 points of the Zariski–Riemann space, via splitting decomposition groups with inertia T^α. Implicitly he is asking whether all sections arise this way. This is a higher-dimensional birational section conjecture phrased via the Zariski–Riemann space, slightly earlier and more general than the usual curve-case formulation attributed to the letter to Faltings.
missed.quote: on trouve des groupes d'inertie à structure simple ... T^α ..., où α est le "codim" de x ∈ 𝓧 correspondant
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is historical evidence that Grothendieck considered the birational section conjecture in higher dimension, with valuations of higher rank (Parshin-chain type) as the expected source of sections. That is the framework of later work by Pop, Koenigsmann and Stix, but its attribution to him in this form is not documented.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is standard ramification theory. The interest is historical: an explicit higher-dimensional, Zariski–Riemann-space version of 'sections come from valuations', which is close to the birational section conjecture programme developed later by others. The section conjecture itself is already credited to Grothendieck.
transcription_corrections: '"cardinal" de x ∈ 𝓗' should likely read '"codim" de x ∈ 𝓧' (the Riemann variety 𝓧).
'des T^α_α ensembles[?]' is probably 'de T^α essentiellement' or similar, with T^α the inertia; the marginal note reads T_α = T_α(L̄) or T_∞ = T_∞(L̄).
'une catégorie de 𝓔^{k(α)}_{k(α)}' probably concerns 𝓔_{k(x)} with residue field k(x), not k(α).
'K-groupe fini ... ouvert de k(α)' likely: 'puisque k(x) est fini sur K' (finite residue extension for dim-0 points).
'choix de pointes[?]' may be 'choix de paramètres'.
'Ceci donne...' continues on the next page as 'Ceci donnerait un principe général ...'.
